clue.text: March past the idiot with a prank

definitions.text: March past the idiot with a prank

parts.note: the month that comes once March has gone by is April
an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone marches past a fool while playing a practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March past' looks like a military parade, but it means the month after March. The whole clue also describes the victim of a joke played on the first of April.
explanation.definitionFit: On the first day of the fourth month, a person duped by a prank is traditionally mocked by this name.

indicators.note: one piece has gone into another, so the short piece sits inside the longer one

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent
I'd written without its apostrophe gives the two letters

explanation.surface: Someone blames an injury on stress that crept in by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' reads as worry, but here it is emphasis on a syllable; 'entered' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An unplanned, unfortunate event is a synonym of a mishap.

clue.text: Colourful phenomena of artist in ribbons

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
ribbons tied in loops are bows

explanation.surface: A painter wrapped up in ribbons is a colourful sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcs of spectral colour seen when sunlight hits raindrops are colourful sky phenomena.

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
a way is a road or street, as in Broadway

explanation.surface: A tax allowance granted to someone living on a sheltered side street.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for manoeuvre or tolerance is a kind of allowance.

clue.text: So upset having phoned for long-armed apes

indicators.note: one piece has another within it, holding it inside
in a down clue, upset means the word so is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: to phone someone is to ring them, past tense rang

explanation.surface: Someone is so upset that they phone about long-armed apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works as a reversal only because this is a down entry, read bottom to top; 'having' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangutans are long-armed great apes, and this is a short form of their name.

clue.text: They get off flights with very old soldiers

definitions.meaning: these weapons let fly arrows, whose feathered ends are flights
medieval archers armed with such weapons were themselves called by the weapon's name

explanation.definitionFit: Tall wooden archery weapons shoot feathered arrows, and old English archers who bore them were named after them.

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first, so it comes after it in the answer

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for softly
to call someone on the phone is to ring them, past tense rang

explanation.surface: A driver called softly after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash, usually in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a collision or accident, especially a minor car smash.

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: only the extreme ends of the word idle are used, its first and last letters

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: A gloomy pall left someone extremely idle once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy curtain hung across a doorway is a draped covering, like a pall.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Essential oils hearten bath salts' (6) for ATTARS: no hidden run, anagram or charade of these words gives ATTARS; the clue appears garbled and no source gives the original

clue.text: Girl that is attendant to Scottish chief

parts.note: Gill is a girl's name
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A girl, that is, waits on a Highland chieftain.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie (or ghillie) is a Scottish attendant, originally to a Highland chief, now usually a hunting or fishing guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland servant or guide who attends a laird on hunting and fishing trips.

clue.text: Ring the gunner — a grotesque monster

parts.note: to ring a bell is to chime
RA, the Royal Artillery, supplies the crossword gunner

explanation.surface: Someone rings an artillery man to report a grotesque monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing beast of Greek myth with lion, goat and serpent parts is a grotesque monster.

clue.text: Time close to starting a trip

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Time close to starting a trip' (9) for NIGHTFALL: NIGHT + FALL fits, but no reading gives every word a job ('close to starting' has none); no source gives the original
annotationWithheld.clue: Time close to starting a trip

indicators.note: the first piece is taken with the second inside it, holding it

parts.note: EMS abbreviates the European Monetary System
pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A European currency scheme names its prices in units of twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is the container signal here. A pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds, a monkey for five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Words derived from people's names, such as sandwich, are a special class of names.

clue.text: Manage to get on and look after

parts.note: on top of something is over it
to see to something is to look after it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get on and look after a household.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct is a synonym of manage.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Overseas tables tests for yahoos!' (9,6) for TASTELESS BEASTS: the anagram is of SEAS TABLES TESTS with 'Over' as indicator, so the one word 'Overseas' does two jobs (indicator and fodder), which cannot be parsed

clue.text: Proof first date Enid would express about

indicators.note: the outer word goes about, surrounding, the inner letters

parts.note: to evince a feeling is to express or show it

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of the two words that follow is used

explanation.surface: Enid would bring up proof of a first date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes D and E from 'date Enid', and 'about' puts them inside EVINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts or signs that support a claim are a synonym of proof.

clue.text: Was not initially tempted to be excused

parts.note: ex means former, what was once so

indicators.note: the word tempted is taken without its initial letter

explanation.surface: Someone who was not tempted at first is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the T of TEMPTED, leaving EMPTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed from a duty or obligation is a synonym of excused.

clue.text: Taking drinks gains good marks for robberies

indicators.note: one piece gains, taking in, the other inside itself

parts.note: one who sups is taking drinks, a sip at a time
a tick is the mark a teacher gives for a good answer

explanation.surface: A pupil who takes drinks still gains good marks for a project on robberies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gains' is the container signal. A tick is the mark a teacher writes beside a correct answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold-ups at gunpoint are a kind of robbery.

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Beaches where the main teams play.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal shores where land meets the ocean are beaches.

parts.note: someone knocked unconscious is out
a side is one division or part of something, as one side of an argument

explanation.surface: A divided crowd sat unconscious at an open-air event.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the open air rather than indoors, as an alfresco meal is.

clue.text: Futile to return ten a spare crust

indicators.note: in this down clue the little word to is made to return, read back to front

parts.note: ten written as the digits 1 and 0 looks like IO

indicators.note: the crust of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: It is futile to send back ten loaves and a spare crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TO into OT, and 'crust' takes S and E, the first and last letters of 'spare'.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving no practical purpose, pointless, is a synonym of futile.

clue.text: It's plain the fish swallowed the physician

indicators.note: one piece has gone into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: tuna is a fish
Dr abbreviates doctor, a physician

explanation.surface: Plainly, the fish swallowed the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's plain' reads as 'clearly', but 'plain' is a flat expanse of land; 'swallowed' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast treeless Arctic expanse with frozen subsoil is a kind of plain.

parts.note: someone forced to do something was made to do it
IRA, the Irish Republican Army, is a rebel army

explanation.surface: A rebel army was forced to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from an Atlantic island of Portugal is a drink.

definitions.meaning: to beach someone is to strand them on a shore, as castaways are left

explanation.definitionFit: Both a dark brownish-red hue and a verb meaning to strand someone on a deserted island.

clue.text: Love to win me over to relegate

parts.note: local here is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub, not local government, so the person in control is the landlord

explanation.surface: A council official in charge of local government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local control' suggests a council; in Britain a 'local' is the pub nearest home.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who runs a pub or tavern is responsible for that hostelry.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Bombastic alternative to being fat' (7) for OROTUND: OR + ROTUND has one R too many and O + ROTUND leaves 'alternative' without a job; no parse gives every word a job and no source gives the original

indicators.note: the first piece is taken with the second held inside it

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
an ad, advertisement, is a bill posted on a wall

explanation.surface: A First Lady dodges the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is the first woman of Genesis; 'with' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid or escape something is a synonym of dodge.

indicators.note: a sorry state is a poor, disordered one, so the letters of Danes are jumbled

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A sorry Danish company employs ballerinas.
explanation.definitionFit: Female ballet dancers are ballerinas.
